content: Each interaction is presented as a clear, standalone statement: 1. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of nilotinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Chloroquine elevates the levels or effects of nortriptyline by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. It also increases nortriptyline toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of octreotide by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 4. Chloroquine and ofatumumab SC may mutually enhance each other's immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Consider the additive effects on the immune system when co-administering immunosuppressive therapies. Monitor closely. 5. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of ofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 6. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of olanzapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Chloroquine and olaparib exhibit pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing toxicity. Co-administration with other myelosuppressive anticancer agents may potentiate and prolong myelosuppressive toxicity. Monitor closely. 8. Chloroquine elevates the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the frequency of oliceridine dosing. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 9. Chloroquine and olodaterol inhaled both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely if unavoidable. 10. Omaveloxolone reduces the systemic exposure of chloroquine by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Omaveloxolone may also reduce systemic exposure of sensitive CYP2C8 substrates. Check prescribing information for dosage adjustments if needed. 11. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of ondansetron by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Chloroquine and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of osimertinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Oxaliplatin increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or the use of an alternative drug. 15. Chloroquine elevates the levels or effects of oxycodone by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. However, it also decreases oxycodone effects by reducing its metabolism, leading to decreased conversion to the active metabolite morphine. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 16. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of oxymorphone by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Chloroquine and ozanimod both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of paliperidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Chloroquine and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat is known to significantly prolong the QT interval, and its prescribing information advises against use with drugs that prolong the QTc interval. 20. Chloroquine elevates the levels or effects of paroxetine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 21. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of pasireotide by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown. 22. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of pazopanib by prolonging the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown. 24. Chloroquine elevates the levels or effects of perhexiline by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 25. Chloroquine elevates the levels of perphenazine by decreasing its metabolism via hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. It also increases perphenazine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of chloroquine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Phenytoin reduces the levels or effects of chloroquine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of pimavanserin by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown. 29. Chloroquine and pimozide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Chloroquine and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Chloroquine reduces the effects of pneumococcal vaccine (13-valent and polyvalent) by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 32. Chloroquine and ponatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Chloroquine also increases the toxicity of posaconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown. 34. Potassium bicarbonate reduces the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate doses by at least 4 hours. 35. Chloroquine reduces the levels of praziquantel by an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Chloroquine and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Additionally, there is a risk of hemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients. Monitor closely. 37. Primidone reduces the levels or effects of chloroquine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of procainamide by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Chloroquine elevates the levels of prochlorperazine by decreasing its metabolism via hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. The clinical significance is unknown. 40. Chloroquine elevates the levels of promethazine by decreasing its metabolism via hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. The clinical significance is unknown. 41. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of propafenone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Chloroquine elevates the levels or effects of propranolol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of prototypical tricyclic antidepressants like protriptyline by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown. 44. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of quetiapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by an unspecified mechanism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of QTc prolongation. 46. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of quinine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 47. Chloroquine reduces the effects of rabies vaccine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 48. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of ranolazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Chloroquine reduces the effects of remdesivir by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 50. Resmetirom increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP2C8 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. This is a partial response due to the extensive length of the original text.
